title: GLP-1 receptor expression within the human heart
authors: Baggio LL, Yusta B, Mulvihill EE, Cao X, Streutker CJ, Butany J, et al.
population: Fifteen human hearts, human pancreas, Brunner's glands and cultured human cardiac fibroblasts, coronary endothelial and vascular smooth muscle cells
funder: Supported by CIHR Foundation Grant 154321, the Canada Research Chairs Program, the Banting and Best Diabetes Centre Novo Nordisk Chair in Incretin Biology, and a grant from Novo Nordisk in support of the cardiovascular mechanisms of GLP-1 action, all to D.J.D.
authorConflicts: D.J.D. reported advisory or consulting roles with Arisaph, Intarcia, Merck, Novo Nordisk and Pfizer within the previous 12 months.
result: Full-length GLP1R mRNA transcripts were detected in all four cardiac chambers of 15 hearts at levels approximating those in human pancreas, and by in situ hybridisation in sinoatrial node tissue; transcripts were absent from cultured cardiac fibroblasts, coronary endothelial and vascular smooth muscle cells. The ventricular cell types that translate the receptor could not be identified; validated antisera lacked sensitivity to detect endogenous receptor protein by Western blotting.
